# Script information

This notebook, developed by the EcoCommons team, showcases how to get species data from different data custodians.

# Introduction

Shorebirds are key indicators of wetland health. This notebook demonstrates how to use `spocc` to fetch and visualise species occurrence data for:

-   **Bar-tailed Godwit (*Limosa lapponica*)**
-   **Red-necked Stint (*Calidris ruficollis*)**
-   **Curlew Sandpiper (*Calidris ferruginea*)**

These are long distance migratory birds which make their way to Australia and Tasmania, we will guide you how to check for species data through multiple available data custodians.

# Set-up: R Environment and Packages

Some housekeeping before we start. This process might take some time as many packages needed to be installed.

## S.1 Set the working directory and create a folder for data.

Save the Quarto Markdown file (.QMD) to a folder of your choice, and then set the path to your folder as your working directory.

```{r}
# Set the workspace to the current working directory
# Uncomment and replace the path below with your own working directory if needed:
# setwd("/Users/zhaoxiang/Documents/tmp/EC_GLM_notebook") 

workspace <- getwd()  # Get the current working directory and store it in 'workspace'

# Increase the plot size by adjusting the options for plot dimensions in the notebook output
options(repr.plot.width = 16, repr.plot.height = 8)  # Sets width to 16 and height to 8 for larger plots

```

## S.2 Install and load essential libraries.

Install and load R packages.

```{r install_libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Set CRAN mirror
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cran.rstudio.com/"))

# List of packages to check, install if needed, and load
packages <- c("spocc", "tidyverse", "leaflet", "sf", "rnaturalearth", "rnaturalearthdata")

# Function to display a cat message
cat_message <- function(pkg, message_type) {
  if (message_type == "installed") {
    cat(paste0(pkg, " has been installed successfully!\n"))
  } else if (message_type == "loading") {
    cat(paste0(pkg, " is already installed and has been loaded!\n"))
  }
}

# Install missing packages and load them
for (pkg in packages) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg)
    cat_message(pkg, "installed")
  } else {
    cat_message(pkg, "loading")
  }
  library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
}

library(spocc)
library(tidyverse)
library(leaflet)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
```

## Step 2 Get data: Listing our Bird species

We use `spocc` to retrieve up to 500 occurrence records per species:

```{r}
# Define species of interest
species_list <- c("Limosa lapponica", "Calidris ruficollis", "Calidris ferruginea")

# Query multiple sources for species occurrences
species_data <- lapply(species_list, function(species) {
  occ(query = species, from = c("gbif", "inat", "obis"), limit = 500)
})

# Convert results to data frames
species_dfs <- lapply(species_data, function(data) occ2df(data$gbif))

# Assign species names
for (i in seq_along(species_dfs)) {
  species_dfs[[i]]$species <- species_list[i]
}

# Combine data into one dataframe
occurrences <- bind_rows(species_dfs)

## Preview Data
for (i in seq_along(species_list)) {
  cat("\nPreview of", species_list[i], "data:\n")
  print(head(species_dfs[[i]], 10))  # Print the first 10 rows of each species' data
}
```

## Step 3 Data Cleaning and Filtering

We remove invalid coordinates and filter occurrences within Australia’s boundary

```{r}
# Remove NA values for latitude and longitude
occurrences_clean <- occurrences %>%
  filter(!is.na(longitude) & !is.na(latitude))

# Load world countries and extract Australia
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
australia <- world %>% filter(admin == "Australia")

# Convert occurrences to a spatial object
occurrences_sf <- st_as_sf(occurrences_clean, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# Filter occurrences for Queensland (approximate using Australia's boundary)
occurrences_aus <- st_intersection(occurrences_sf, australia)

# Print summary of filtered data
print(nrow(occurrences_aus))
print(head(occurrences_aus))
```

## Step 4 Data Visualisation

We assign **EcoCommons theme colors** for better visualization.

```{r}
# Define EcoCommons theme colors
ec_colors <- c("#509E2F", "#2F6C99", "#F39200") # Green, Blue, Orange

# Assign a color to each species
occurrences_aus$color <- factor(occurrences_aus$species, labels = ec_colors)

# Create an interactive map using Leaflet
leaflet(data = occurrences_aus) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    ~longitude, ~latitude, 
    radius = 3, color = ~color, 
    popup = ~species
  ) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
  addLegend(
    "bottomright", 
    colors = ec_colors, 
    labels = species_list, 
    title = "Species"
  )

```

## Step 5 Save data for Analysis

We save the cleaned data in **CSV and Shapefile formats** for additional modeling and GIS analysis.

```{r}
# Save cleaned occurrence data to CSV
write.csv(occurrences_aus, "shorebird_occurrences_AUS.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Save spatial data as a shapefile (if needed)

# Ensure that occurrences_aus is an sf object
if (!inherits(occurrences_aus, "sf")) {
  occurrences_aus <- st_as_sf(occurrences_aus, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)
  cat("Data has been converted to an sf object.\n")
} else {
  cat("Data is already an sf object.\n")
}

# Check the structure of the sf object
print(st_geometry_type(occurrences_aus))  # Should print "POINT" if it's a point geometry

# Now, try writing the shapefile
st_write(occurrences_aus, "shorebird_occurrences_AUS.shp", delete_layer = TRUE)

```
